scale.source: CLDR 48 RBNF hu %spellout-cardinal, ICU 78 rendering of 1000000000: "egymilliárd"; CLDR 48 RBNF hu %spellout-cardinal, ICU 78 rendering of 1000000000000: "egybillió"; CLDR 48 RBNF hu %spellout-cardinal, ICU 78 rendering of 1000000000000000: "egybilliárd": "milliárd" is 10^9 and "billió" 10^12, the long scale.

group_mark.source: Wikipedia, "Hungarian orthography" (knowledge/wiki/audits/numtag/lang-ports/uralic-turkic/sources/wikipedia-Hungarian_orthography.wikitext): "Numerals of more than four digits are divided by spaces (or by dots), in groups of three"; CLDR 48 hu: group U+00A0.

decimal_mark.source: Wikipedia, "Hungarian orthography" (knowledge/wiki/audits/numtag/lang-ports/uralic-turkic/sources/wikipedia-Hungarian_orthography.wikitext): "The beginning of decimal fractions is marked with a comma."

scale_noun_agrees.source: Wiktionary, "három" (knowledge/wiki/audits/numtag/lang-ports/uralic-turkic/sources/wikt-hu-három.wikitext): "Három könyvet vettem." (I bought three books): the noun after a count keeps one form for every count, so "egymillió" and "kétmillió" use the same scale word.

plural_scale_needs_count.source: Hungarian scale words have no plural form after a count ("kétmillió"); the setting matters for no entry.

joiner_tens_units.source: Wikipedia, "Hungarian orthography" (knowledge/wiki/audits/numtag/lang-ports/uralic-turkic/sources/wikipedia-Hungarian_orthography.wikitext): "If cardinal numbers are written in letters, they should be written as one word up to 2000 (e.g. ezerkilencszázkilencvenkilenc '1,999') and they should be divided by hyphens by the usual three-digit division over 2000 (e.g. kétezer-egy '2,001')"

joiner_after_hundred.source: Wikipedia, "Hungarian orthography" (knowledge/wiki/audits/numtag/lang-ports/uralic-turkic/sources/wikipedia-Hungarian_orthography.wikitext): "If cardinal numbers are written in letters, they should be written as one word up to 2000 (e.g. ezerkilencszázkilencvenkilenc '1,999') and they should be divided by hyphens by the usual three-digit division over 2000 (e.g. kétezer-egy '2,001')"

joiner_between_groups.source: Wikipedia, "Hungarian orthography" (knowledge/wiki/audits/numtag/lang-ports/uralic-turkic/sources/wikipedia-Hungarian_orthography.wikitext): "If cardinal numbers are written in letters, they should be written as one word up to 2000 (e.g. ezerkilencszázkilencvenkilenc '1,999') and they should be divided by hyphens by the usual three-digit division over 2000 (e.g. kétezer-egy '2,001')"

joiner_before_round_hundred.source: No joiner stands after the thousands (joiner_between_groups is never): CLDR 48 RBNF hu %spellout-cardinal, ICU 78 rendering of 1500: "ezerötszáz"; CLDR 48 RBNF hu %spellout-cardinal, ICU 78 rendering of 1020: "ezerhúsz".

ordinal_style.source: Hungarian ordinals are entries with "ordinal": true; only the last element is ordinal ("huszonötödik", CLDR 48 RBNF hu %spellout-ordinal, ICU 78 rendering of 25: "huszonötödik").

compound_words.source: Wikipedia, "Hungarian orthography" (knowledge/wiki/audits/numtag/lang-ports/uralic-turkic/sources/wikipedia-Hungarian_orthography.wikitext): "If cardinal numbers are written in letters, they should be written as one word up to 2000 (e.g. ezerkilencszázkilencvenkilenc '1,999') and they should be divided by hyphens by the usual three-digit division over 2000 (e.g. kétezer-egy '2,001')"

inflection_position.source: Wikipedia, "Hungarian orthography" (knowledge/wiki/audits/numtag/lang-ports/uralic-turkic/sources/wikipedia-Hungarian_orthography.wikitext): "Words containing a suffixed numeral are written as one word (e.g. húszméteres út)"; a case ending goes on the last element of a number ("kétezer-ötszázat").

fraction_agreement.source: Wiktionary, "negyed" (knowledge/wiki/audits/numtag/lang-ports/uralic-turkic/sources/wikt-hu-negyed.wikitext): "{{cot|hu|egész|fél|nyolcad|tizenhatod|harmincketted}}"; Wiktionary, "három" (knowledge/wiki/audits/numtag/lang-ports/uralic-turkic/sources/wikt-hu-három.wikitext): "Három könyvet vettem" (I bought three books): a noun after a numeral keeps the singular, so "két harmad" has no plural form.

decimal_fraction.source: Wiktionary, "egész" (knowledge/wiki/audits/numtag/lang-ports/uralic-turkic/sources/wikt-hu-egész.wikitext): "(arithmetic) Names the integer part of a decimal fraction, when it is spoken out loud": "egy egész hét tized" is "one point seven"; the digits after the point are a count of tenths, hundredths or thousandths ("tized", "század", "ezred").

dot_ordinal.source: Wikipedia, "Hungarian orthography" (knowledge/wiki/audits/numtag/lang-ports/uralic-turkic/sources/wikipedia-Hungarian_orthography.wikitext): "Ordinal numbers written in digits take a full stop (e.g. 3. sor '3rd line')".

joiner.source: "és" (and) joins a half to a number ("két és fél"); no conjunction joins the parts of a number (Wikipedia, "Hungarian orthography" (knowledge/wiki/audits/numtag/lang-ports/uralic-turkic/sources/wikipedia-Hungarian_orthography.wikitext): "If cardinal numbers are written in letters, they should be written as one word up to 2000 (e.g. ezerkilencszázkilencvenkilenc '1,999') and they should be divided by hyphens by the usual three-digit division over 2000 (e.g. kétezer-egy '2,001')").

decimal_marker.source: Wiktionary, "egész" (knowledge/wiki/audits/numtag/lang-ports/uralic-turkic/sources/wikt-hu-egész.wikitext): "whole"; Hungarian reads 5.2 as "öt egész két tized", five wholes and two tenths.

minus.source: CLDR 48 RBNF hu %spellout-cardinal renders -5 as "mínusz öt"; "minusz" is the spelling without the accent.

minus_idioms.source: No Hungarian idiom puts "mínusz" before a positive number.

article_one.source: Wiktionary, "egy" (knowledge/wiki/audits/numtag/lang-ports/uralic-turkic/sources/wikt-hu-egy.wikitext): "a, an (indefinite article)": "egy csepp a tengerben", a drop in the ocean.

of.source: Hungarian has no word that multiplies a scale word.

fraction_of.source: Hungarian puts no word between a fraction and a collective.

denominator_particle.source: Hungarian has no particle like Portuguese "avos".

class_noun.source: Hungarian has no class noun after a collective.

half_unit.source: Hungarian puts "fél" before the unit ("fél kiló").

abbreviation.source: No Hungarian number word is also an abbreviation with a period.

lone_decimal_mark.source: Wikipedia, "Hungarian orthography" (knowledge/wiki/audits/numtag/lang-ports/uralic-turkic/sources/wikipedia-Hungarian_orthography.wikitext): "The beginning of decimal fractions is marked with a comma", so ",5" is 0.5.

range_cue.source: Hungarian puts "között" (between) after the numbers, as a postposition ("kettő és öt között"); no word before a range opens it.

digit_suffix_mark.source: Wikipedia, "Hungarian orthography" (knowledge/wiki/audits/numtag/lang-ports/uralic-turkic/sources/wikipedia-Hungarian_orthography.wikitext): "The full stop is retained even before the hyphen that connects suffixes (e.g. a 10.-kel)": a hyphen joins a suffix to digits, and the suffix is no number word.
